docRequirement: hooks.md § FileChanged input: "In addition to the common input fields, FileChanged hooks receive `file_path` and `event`" — `file_path` is the "Absolute path to the file that changed" and `event` is "`\"change\"` for a modified file, `\"add\"` for a created file, or `\"unlink\"` for a deleted file". The JSON example on the page shows exactly those two keys alongside the common fields. The event itself "Runs when a watched file changes on disk", has no decision control, and its matcher both builds the literal watch list and filters on the changed file's basename.
current: The only emitter of FileChanged is the Pi lifecycle bridge. It fires on successful completion of a file-mutating TOOL, not on a disk watch: `FILE_MUTATING_TOOLS = new Set(['write','edit','replace_in_file','multi_edit'])` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:52); the tool's path argument is stashed on `tool_execution_start` (lifecycle-bridge.ts:194-197, via `mutatedPath` at :85-89, which reads `record.path ?? record.file_path ?? record.filePath`) and replayed on `tool_execution_end` (lifecycle-bridge.ts:224-233) as `await options.emit('FileChanged', { hook_event_name: 'FileChanged', change_kind: toolName, ...(path ? { path } : {}) })`. So the payload carries `change_kind` (the tool name, e.g. `write`) and `path`, never `file_path` and never `event`. The path is passed through verbatim with no `resolve()` — there is no `node:path` import in the file (only a `.join('\n')` on an array at lifecycle-bridge.ts:135) — so it is absolute only if the model happened to pass an absolute argument, and it is omitted entirely when the start/end correlation captured nothing. Nothing downstream re-keys it: the payload crosses the subprocess wire as `OutboundAutomationEvent` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:498, sent at :1969 and :2958), is forwarded verbatim by pi-agent.ts:2325 → `BaseAgent.emitAutomationEvent` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:1438-1459) → `dispatchAutomationAgentEvent` (packages/shared/src/automations/lifecycle-hook-dispatcher.ts:14-29), and reaches a command hook's stdin through `hookCommandStdinPayload`, which spreads `...input` and adds only `hook_event_name` and `cwd` (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:641-651). The type declares the fork's spelling: `path?: string; change_kind?: string;` under "Filesystem change events" (packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:804-805), and the frozen contract row declares `redactedPayload: ['change_kind']` (packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:73). The one place that knows the documented spelling is read-side only: `changedFileBasename` reads `input.file_path ?? input.path` (packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:150-154), used by `getMatchValueForSdkInput`'s `case 'FileChanged'` (utils.ts:218-220), so the matcher works today purely through the `?? input.path` fallback. The shape is frozen by tests: packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.test.ts:90 asserts `toEqual({ hook_event_name: 'FileChanged', change_kind: 'write', path: '/repo/sub/a.txt' })`, packages/shared/src/automations/conditions.test.ts:641-643 and packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/hooks-automation.test.ts:621-624 build inputs with `path`/`change_kind`.
divergence: Two documented keys are wrong or missing on the FileChanged stdin payload. (1) Key name only: the absolute-path field is spelled `path`, the doc spells it `file_path` — the value is the same idea, so this is a rename, except that our value is not guaranteed absolute (no `resolve()` against the session cwd) and is absent when uncorrelated. (2) Missing field: `event` (`change`|`add`|`unlink`) is never emitted at all, and the extra `change_kind` (the mutating tool name) is a Nessy invention with no documented counterpart. Because `hookCommandStdinPayload` spreads the input verbatim, a hook doing `jq -r .file_path` reads `null` and `jq -r .event` reads `null`. Separately, and narrower than the doc rather than contradicting a field: the trigger is tool completion over four write tools, not a filesystem watch, so `unlink` is structurally unreachable (a deletion, or any edit made by bash/an external editor, never fires the event), the matcher never builds a watch list, and the documented `watchPaths` output field is unimplemented anywhere in src (`grep -ran watchPaths packages/*/src apps/electron/src` returns nothing).

(b) Import `resolve` from `node:path` and `existsSync` from `node:fs` (the file currently imports neither; it runs in the Node subprocess so both are available). blastRadius: Crosses a wire boundary: the payload travels the pi-agent-server → host subprocess IPC as `OutboundAutomationEvent` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:498, sent at :1969 and :2958) and is consumed by packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:2325. That is a risk trigger in this repo, mitigated by both sides shipping in one bundle (apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server) with no persisted or versioned copy of the payload — nothing writes FileChanged inputs to disk, and `redactedPayload` is a documentation table with no runtime reader (`grep -rn redactedPayload` over src hits only packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts). Readers of the payload: `changedFileBasename` → `getMatchValueForSdkInput` (packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:150-154, :218-220) → `matcherMatchesSdk` (:362-368) → `pluginMatcherMatches` (packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:326-337); the stdin serializer `hookCommandStdinPayload` (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:641-651); the condition evaluator, which sees the whole input as `payload` (utils.ts:365). Imported-plugin path: FileChanged is an accepted hook event for both adapters (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:144 and :163, packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:393, packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-runtime.ts:46 and :179), so a Claude or Codex plugin's `hooks.json` reaches this payload unchanged; note that hooks-automation.ts:316-324 (`externalHookInput`) is the established precedent for re-spelling an input key at the imported-hook boundary if a fork-local spelling ever has to be preserved. Tests that pin the shape: packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.test.ts:90, packages/shared/src/automations/conditions.test.ts:641-643, packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/hooks-automation.test.ts:621-624; the event-name inventories at packages/pi-agent-server/src/__tests__/extension-first/fixtures/behavior-corpus.json:915/:977 and packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/format-adapters.test.ts:3694 list the name only and are unaffected. Trap avoided: the ~15 other `input.path` reads in packages/shared (pre-tool-use.ts, mode-manager.ts, file-checkpoints.ts, lsp-service.ts, SessionManager.ts) are tool-argument records in the permissions/tools subsystems, not `SdkAutomationInput` — only utils.ts:151 reads this one. docs-site/content/automations/overview.md:292 and its ru twin describe the event ("A file mutation completes") but document no payload fields, so they need no change for the rename — though they are where the tool-completion trigger is honestly stated and should stay that way.
userImpact: Observable, and it makes an imported Claude plugin look broken rather than absent. Install a Claude plugin whose `hooks.json` declares a FileChanged hook — the documented example shape is a `.envrc`/`.env` reloader, and formatter-on-save hooks are the same pattern — then have the agent write that file with the write/edit tool. The hook DOES fire and its matcher DOES match (the basename comes from the `path` fallback), so the user sees the hook run and any stderr surface; but the script's `jq -r .file_path` (or `$file_path`) yields the string `null`, so it formats nothing, reloads nothing, or errors on a path named "null". Any `event`-conditional branch (`if [ "$event" = "add" ]`) never takes, since the key is absent on every emission. A user writing their own Nessy automation from our docs hits the same wall from the other side: docs-site documents the event but no fields, so copying a Claude example is the natural move. Latent parts, for honesty: deleting a file, editing one through bash, or an external editor touching a watched file produces no event at all — that surfaces only for a user who expects a real disk watcher, and no `watchPaths`-returning hook can work at all today.
